questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing term in the series: 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, ?

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next number in the series: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing letter in the series: B, D, G, K, P, ?
questions.explanation: The gap between consecutive letters increases by 1 each time: B(+2)D(+3)G(+4)K(+5)P(+6)V, i.e., positions 2,4,7,11,16,22 which is B,D,G,K,P,V.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Doctor is to Hospital as Teacher is to:
questions.explanation: A doctor's usual place of work is a hospital; similarly, a teacher's usual place of work is a school.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Thermometer is to Temperature as Barometer is to:
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature; a barometer measures atmospheric pressure — both are measuring instruments paired with the quantity they measure.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Find the odd one out: Copper, Iron, Aluminium, Sulphur
questions.explanation: Copper, Iron and Aluminium are all metals, whereas Sulphur is a non-metal.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Find the odd one out: 16, 25, 36, 49, 52
questions.explanation: 16, 25, 36 and 49 are all perfect squares (4², 5², 6², 7²); 52 is not a perfect square.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: In a certain code, TABLE is written as UBCMF. How will CHAIR be written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter of TABLE is shifted one place forward in the alphabet (T→U, A→B, B→C, L→M, E→F) to give UBCMF. Applying the same rule to CHAIR: C→D, H→I, A→B, I→J, R→S, giving DIBJS.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: If in a certain language MANGO is coded as OCPIQ, how will PAPER be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted two places forward in the alphabet (M→O, A→C, N→P, G→I, O→Q) to give OCPIQ. Applying the same shift to PAPER: P→R, A→C, P→R, E→G, R→T, giving RCRGT.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Pointing to a man, a woman said, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of the woman's mother is the woman herself. So the man's mother is the woman, meaning the woman is the man's mother.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: P is Q's father. Q is R's sister. S is R's mother. How is P related to S?
questions.explanation: P is the father of Q, and R is Q's sibling, so P is also R's father. S is R's mother. Since P and S are the parents of the same children, P is S's husband.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A man walks 5 km towards north, then turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: North 5 km, then right (east) 3 km, then right again (south) 5 km brings him back to the original latitude but 3 km east of the start, so the net distance is 3 km, due east.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Ravi walks 8 km towards south, then turns left and walks 6 km, then turns left again and walks 8 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: South 8 km, then left (east) 6 km, then left again (north) 8 km cancels the southward displacement, leaving a net displacement of 6 km to the east.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Five friends D, C, E, B and A are sitting in a row facing north. D sits third to the left of B. A sits at one of the extreme ends. E sits second to the right of D. Only two people sit between A and C. Who sits at the extreme right end?
questions.explanation: Placing D at position 1 and B at position 4 (third to the left of B), E second to the right of D gives E at position 3, leaving C at position 2. A must occupy the remaining extreme end, position 5, giving the order D-C-E-B-A, which also satisfies 'two people between A and C' (E and B lie between them).

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: If '+' means '÷', '−' means '×', '×' means '+', and '÷' means '−', find the value of: 20 + 4 − 3 × 6 ÷ 2
questions.explanation: Substituting the new meanings: 20÷4×3+6−2. By BODMAS: 20÷4=5; 5×3=15; 15+6=21; 21−2=19.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Which letter is the 5th letter to the right of the 13th letter from the left in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: The 13th letter from the left is M. Counting 5 letters to the right of M: N, O, P, Q, R — the 5th letter is R.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: If 1 January 2024 was a Monday, what day of the week was 1 January 2025?
questions.explanation: 2024 is a leap year with 366 days. 366 ÷ 7 leaves a remainder of 2, so the day of the week advances by 2 from Monday, landing on Wednesday.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 60 years. Six years ago, the father's age was 5 times the son's age. What is the present age of the father?
questions.explanation: Let the son's present age be x, so the father's is 60−x. Six years ago: 60−x−6 = 5(x−6) ⟹ 54−x = 5x−30 ⟹ 84 = 6x ⟹ x=14. The father's present age is 60−14 = 46 years.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Statements: All pens are books. All books are papers. Conclusions: I. All pens are papers. II. Some papers are pens. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: Since all pens are books and all books are papers, it directly follows that all pens are papers (I). Since at least one pen exists and every pen is a paper, it also follows that some papers are pens (II).

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: In a class of 40 students, Ravi's rank from the top is 14th. What is his rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation: Rank from the bottom = Total students − Rank from top + 1 = 40 − 14 + 1 = 27th.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which blood group is known as the 'universal donor'?
questions.explanation: O negative red blood cells lack A, B and Rh antigens, so they can be transfused to recipients of almost any blood group in an emergency, earning the name 'universal donor'.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Deficiency of which vitamin causes night blindness?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is essential for the formation of rhodopsin, the pigment in retinal rod cells needed for vision in dim light; its deficiency causes night blindness (nyctalopia).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: The skin, covering the entire external surface of the body, is the largest organ by both surface area and weight.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which hormone is commonly known as the 'fight or flight' hormone?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline (epinephrine), secreted by the adrenal medulla, prepares the body for sudden physical action by increasing heart rate, blood pressure and blood glucose — the 'fight or flight' response.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The human heart has four chambers: two upper atria and two lower ventricles.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Right to Constitutional Remedies is guaranteed under which Article of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 32 empowers citizens to directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights; Dr B.R. Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: As per Article 64 of the Constitution, the Vice President of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: What is the minimum age required to become a member of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: As per Article 84 of the Constitution, a person must be at least 25 years of age to be eligible for membership of the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in which year?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Dandi March on 12 March 1930 to protest the British salt tax, marking a major milestone of the civil disobedience movement.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Who founded the Maurya Empire?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 322 BCE, with guidance from his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Battle of Plassey, which laid the foundation of British rule in India, was fought in which year?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 between the British East India Company under Robert Clive and Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Who was the first and only Indian to hold the post of Governor-General of independent India?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten was the first Governor-General of independent India (1947–48); C. Rajagopalachari succeeded him and remains the only Indian to have held the post.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of these Indian states?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram, but not through Kerala, which lies further south.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which is the largest state of India by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan, covering about 3.42 lakh sq km, is the largest Indian state by area.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Thar Desert, the largest hot desert in India, is located mainly in which state?
questions.explanation: The Thar Desert (Great Indian Desert) lies mainly in the state of Rajasthan, extending partly into Gujarat, Punjab and Haryana.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Tughlaqabad Fort in Delhi was built by which ruler?
questions.explanation: Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq, founder of the Tughlaq dynasty, built Tughlaqabad Fort in Delhi in the early 14th century as his capital.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The first line of the Delhi Metro became operational in which year?
questions.explanation: The Delhi Metro's first section, the Red Line between Shahdara and Tis Hazari, opened to the public on 24 December 2002.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Rajghat in Delhi is a memorial dedicated to which national leader?
questions.explanation: Rajghat is the site of Mahatma Gandhi's cremation on the banks of the Yamuna and serves as his memorial.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The term 'Chinaman', referring to a type of left-arm wrist-spin bowling, is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: In cricket, a 'Chinaman' is a delivery bowled by a left-arm bowler using a wrist-spin (unorthodox) action, spinning the ball into a right-handed batsman.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Kathak, a classical dance form marked by intricate footwork and pirouettes, originated in which region of India?
questions.explanation: Kathak originated in North India, particularly associated with the storytelling traditions of temples and later royal courts of Rajasthan and Awadh.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: The average of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 61. Find the largest of these numbers.
questions.explanation: For 5 consecutive odd numbers, the average equals the middle number, so the middle number is 61. The numbers are 57, 59, 61, 63, 65, making the largest 65.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: In an election between two candidates, the winner secured 65% of the votes and won by 6000 votes. Find the total number of votes polled.
questions.explanation: The winner's margin corresponds to 65%−35% = 30% of the total votes. So 30% of total = 6000 ⟹ total = 6000/0.30 = 20,000.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: A shopkeeper sells an article at a 20% profit. Had he bought it for 10% less and sold it for ₹63 less, he would have gained 25%. Find the cost price of the article.
questions.explanation: Let CP = x. Original SP = 1.2x. New CP = 0.9x, and new SP = 1.25 × 0.9x = 1.125x. Given original SP − new SP = 63: 1.2x − 1.125x = 0.075x = 63 ⟹ x = 840.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 3:5. If 10 is added to each, the ratio becomes 5:7. Find the two numbers.
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be 3x and 5x. Then (3x+10)/(5x+10) = 5/7 ⟹ 21x+70 = 25x+50 ⟹ 4x = 20 ⟹ x = 5. The numbers are 15 and 25.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: Find the simple interest on ₹12,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: Find the compound interest on ₹8,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 12 days and B can complete it in 18 days. In how many days will they complete the work together?
questions.explanation: A's one-day work = 1/12, B's one-day work = 1/18. Combined = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36. Time taken together = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: A train 150 m long running at 60 km/hr crosses a platform 250 m long. How long does it take?
questions.explanation: Total distance to cover = 150 + 250 = 400 m. Speed = 60 km/hr = 60 × 5/18 = 50/3 m/s. Time = 400 ÷ (50/3) = 400 × 3/50 = 24 seconds.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 12 and 336 respectively. If one of the numbers is 48, find the other number.
questions.explanation: For two numbers, HCF × LCM = product of the numbers. So the other number = (12 × 336)/48 = 4032/48 = 84.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: The population of a town increases by 10% every year. If its current population is 1,21,000, what was its population 2 years ago?
questions.explanation: Population 2 years ago × (1.1)² = 1,21,000 ⟹ Population 2 years ago = 1,21,000 / 1.21 = 1,00,000.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: If A:B = 2:3 and B:C = 4:5, find A:B:C.
questions.explanation: Make B's value common: A:B = 2:3 = 8:12, and B:C = 4:5 = 12:15 (multiplying to make B = 12 in both). Combining gives A:B:C = 8:12:15.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: The average weight of 8 men increases by 1.5 kg when a new man replaces one of them weighing 65 kg. Find the weight of the new man.
questions.explanation: Total weight increases by 8 × 1.5 = 12 kg. So the new man's weight = 65 + 12 = 77 kg.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: A man sold two articles, each for ₹1,200. On one he gained 20% and on the other he lost 20%. Find his overall gain or loss percentage.
questions.explanation: When the selling price of two articles is equal and the profit and loss percentages are equal in magnitude, there is always a net loss, given by (common%)²/100 = 20²/100 = 4% loss.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: 15 men can complete a piece of work in 20 days. How many men are needed to complete the same work in 12 days?
questions.explanation: Using men × days = constant: 15 × 20 = M × 12 ⟹ M = 300/12 = 25 men.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: A boat covers 30 km downstream in 2 hours and the same distance upstream in 3 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 30/2 = 15 km/hr; upstream speed = 30/3 = 10 km/hr. Speed in still water = (15+10)/2 = 12.5 km/hr.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 10% per annum is ₹150. Find the sum.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: Find the greatest number that divides 245 and 1029, leaving a remainder of 5 in each case.
questions.explanation: Subtracting the remainder: 245−5=240 and 1029−5=1024. The required number is HCF(240, 1024). Since 240 = 2⁴×3×5 and 1024 = 2¹⁰, HCF = 2⁴ = 16.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: Find the average of the first 50 natural numbers.
questions.explanation: Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n+1)/2 = 50×51/2 = 1275. Average = 1275/50 = 25.5.

questions.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
questions.question: A number is first increased by 25% and then decreased by 20%. Find the net percentage change.
questions.explanation: Net multiplying factor = 1.25 × 0.80 = 1.00, meaning the number returns to its original value — a net change of 0%.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the word most nearly similar in meaning to 'AUDACIOUS':
questions.explanation: 'Audacious' means showing a willingness to take bold risks, which is closest in meaning to 'daring'.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to 'BENEVOLENT':
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and kindly; its direct opposite is 'malevolent', meaning having or showing ill will.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To beat around the bush'
options: To avoid speaking directly about something
questions.explanation: 'To beat around the bush' means to avoid talking about the main point directly, often to delay discussing something unpleasant.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the correct one-word substitute for: 'A person who is unable to read or write'
questions.explanation: 'Illiterate' precisely means a person who cannot read or write.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Spot the error in the sentence: 'Neither of the two boys (a) / were present (b) / in the class (c) / No error (d)'
questions.explanation: 'Neither...nor' constructions take a singular verb. Since 'neither' refers to one of the two boys, the verb should be 'was present', not 'were present'.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition: 'He has been living in Delhi ___ 2015.'
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time (a starting year like 2015) to indicate an action continuing from that point to the present.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the correct improvement for the underlined part: 'She don't like to travel alone.'
questions.explanation: The subject 'She' is third person singular, so the auxiliary verb must be 'doesn't', not 'don't': 'She doesn't like to travel alone.'

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the word most nearly similar in meaning to 'METICULOUS':
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise, which is closest to 'careful'.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to 'TRANSPARENT':
questions.explanation: 'Transparent' means allowing light to pass through so objects can be seen clearly; its opposite is 'opaque', meaning not able to be seen through.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To bite the bullet'
options: To face a difficult situation bravely
questions.explanation: 'To bite the bullet' means to accept and face something difficult or unpleasant with courage.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the correct one-word substitute for: 'A place where birds are kept'
questions.explanation: An 'aviary' is a large enclosure specifically built for keeping birds.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Spot the error in the sentence: 'Each of the students (a) / have submitted (b) / their assignment (c) / No error (d)'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is a singular pronoun and always takes a singular verb, so it should be 'has submitted', not 'have submitted'.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate verb: 'The committee ___ divided in its opinion.'
questions.explanation: 'Committee' is a collective noun that is treated as singular when acting as one unit, so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the correct improvement for the underlined part: 'If I was you, I would accept the offer.'
questions.explanation: In hypothetical/unreal conditional sentences, the subjunctive mood requires 'were' for all persons: 'If I were you, I would accept the offer.'

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the word most nearly similar in meaning to 'ZEALOUS':
questions.explanation: 'Zealous' means showing great energy or enthusiasm in pursuit of a cause or objective, closest in meaning to 'enthusiastic'.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to 'FRUGAL':
questions.explanation: 'Frugal' means sparing or economical with money or resources; its opposite is 'extravagant', meaning spending money lavishly.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To hit the nail on the head'
options: To finish a task in a hurry
To describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem
questions.explanation: 'To hit the nail on the head' means to describe or identify a problem or situation with great accuracy.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the correct one-word substitute for: 'One who cannot be corrected'
questions.explanation: 'Incorrigible' describes a person or habit that cannot be corrected, improved, or reformed.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Spot the error in the sentence: 'He is one of the best (a) / player in the team (b) / who has ever played (c) / No error (d)'
options: He is one of the best
questions.explanation: The phrase 'one of the best' must be followed by a plural noun, so it should read 'one of the best players in the team', not 'player'.

questions.subject: English Language & Comprehension
questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition: 'She has been working here ___ five years.'
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a duration or period of time (like 'five years'), while 'since' is used with a specific starting point in time.

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से 'जल' का पर्यायवाची शब्द नहीं है:
questions.explanation: 'पवन' का अर्थ है 'हवा', जो 'जल' का पर्यायवाची नहीं है। नीर, वारि और पानी — तीनों 'जल' के मान्य पर्यायवाची हैं।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से 'आकाश' का पर्यायवाची शब्द नहीं है:
questions.explanation: 'धरा' का अर्थ है 'पृथ्वी', जबकि गगन, अंबर और नभ — तीनों 'आकाश' के पर्यायवाची हैं।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: 'सुख' का विलोम शब्द है:
questions.explanation: 'सुख' का सीधा विलोम (विपरीतार्थक) शब्द 'दुःख' है।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: 'उन्नति' का विलोम शब्द है:
questions.explanation: 'उन्नति' (तरक्की/उत्थान) का विलोम शब्द 'अवनति' (पतन) है।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: मुहावरा 'दाल में कुछ काला होना' का सही अर्थ है:
questions.explanation: 'दाल में कुछ काला होना' मुहावरे का अर्थ है किसी बात या मामले में कुछ संदेहास्पद या गड़बड़ होने का आभास होना।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: मुहावरा 'चादर से बाहर पैर पसारना' का सही अर्थ है:
options: अपनी सामर्थ्य से अधिक खर्च करना
questions.explanation: 'चादर से बाहर पैर पसारना' मुहावरे का अर्थ है अपनी आय या सामर्थ्य से अधिक खर्च करना।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: 'जिसे जीता न जा सके' के लिए एक शब्द है:
questions.explanation: 'जिसे जीता न जा सके' का अर्थ बताने वाला एक शब्द है 'अजेय'।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: 'जो कम बोलता हो' के लिए एक शब्द है:
questions.explanation: 'जो कम बोलता हो' के लिए प्रयुक्त एक शब्द है 'मितभाषी'। ('मृदुभाषी' का अर्थ है मीठा बोलने वाला, कम बोलने वाला नहीं।)

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: निम्नलिखित वाक्य का शुद्ध रूप चुनिए: 'राम ने पुस्तक पढ़ा।'
questions.explanation: 'पुस्तक' शब्द स्त्रीलिंग है, इसलिए क्रिया भी स्त्रीलिंग होनी चाहिए — 'पढ़ी', 'पढ़ा' नहीं। अतः शुद्ध वाक्य है 'राम ने पुस्तक पढ़ी।'

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: 'सूर्योदय' शब्द में कौन-सी संधि है?
questions.explanation: 'सूर्य + उदय' में 'अ' और 'उ' मिलकर 'ओ' बनता है (अ+उ=ओ), जो गुण संधि का नियम है। अतः यह गुण संधि (स्वर संधि का एक भेद) है।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: 'राजपुत्र' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: 'राजपुत्र' का अर्थ है 'राजा का पुत्र', जिसमें कारक विभक्ति का लोप होता है — यह तत्पुरुष समास का उदाहरण है।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: 'अग्नि' शब्द का तद्भव रूप है:
questions.explanation: 'अग्नि' तत्सम शब्द है और इसका तद्भव (परिवर्तित हिंदी) रूप 'आग' है।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: 'दुग्ध' शब्द का तद्भव रूप है:
questions.explanation: 'दुग्ध' तत्सम शब्द है और इसका तद्भव रूप 'दूध' है।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: 'लड़का' शब्द का बहुवचन रूप क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'लड़का' (एकवचन, पुल्लिंग) का सही बहुवचन रूप 'लड़के' है; 'लड़कों' का प्रयोग कारक चिह्न के साथ किया जाता है, जैसे 'लड़कों को'।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द स्त्रीलिंग है?
questions.explanation: 'नदी' शब्द स्त्रीलिंग है, जबकि पर्वत, समुद्र और आकाश — तीनों पुल्लिंग शब्द हैं।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से 'पवन' का पर्यायवाची शब्द नहीं है:
questions.explanation: 'अनल' का अर्थ है 'अग्नि', जो 'पवन' (हवा) का पर्यायवाची नहीं है। वायु, समीर और अनिल — तीनों 'पवन' के पर्यायवाची हैं।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: 'आरंभ' का विलोम शब्द है:
questions.explanation: 'आरंभ' (शुरुआत) का विलोम शब्द 'अंत' (समाप्ति) है।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: मुहावरा 'ईद का चाँद होना' का सही अर्थ है:
questions.explanation: 'ईद का चाँद होना' मुहावरे का अर्थ है बहुत लंबे समय के बाद किसी का दिखाई देना।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: 'जिसका कोई शत्रु न हो' के लिए एक शब्द है:
questions.explanation: 'जिसका कोई शत्रु न हो' के लिए प्रयुक्त उपयुक्त एक शब्द 'अजातशत्रु' है।

questions.subject: Hindi Language & Comprehension
questions.question: 'नीलकमल' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: 'नीलकमल' का अर्थ है 'नीला कमल', जिसमें विशेषण-विशेष्य का संबंध है — यह कर्मधारय समास का उदाहरण है।

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The xiphisternal joint, an important surface landmark in chest and abdominal positioning, lies opposite which vertebral level?
questions.explanation: The xiphisternal joint (junction of the body of the sternum and the xiphoid process) is a standard positioning landmark that lies opposite the T9–T10 vertebral level.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: How many bones make up the adult human skeleton?
questions.explanation: The adult human skeleton normally consists of 206 bones (infants have more, around 270, many of which fuse together during growth).

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The carina, the point at which the trachea bifurcates into the right and left main bronchi, lies at approximately which vertebral level?
questions.explanation: The carina lies at approximately the T4–T5 vertebral level, roughly the same level as the sternal angle (angle of Louis), which is used clinically as a corresponding anterior landmark.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which bone is the largest and strongest bone in the human lower limb, responsible for weight-bearing?
questions.explanation: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest, largest and strongest bone in the body, transmitting body weight from the hip to the knee.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The iliac crest, a key palpable landmark for pelvis and lumbar spine positioning, lies approximately at the level of which lumbar vertebra?
questions.explanation: The iliac crest is a standard palpable landmark that lies approximately at the level of the L4 vertebra (or the L4–L5 disc space), commonly used to localise the lumbar spine.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which chamber of the heart receives oxygenated blood from the lungs via the pulmonary veins?
questions.explanation: The left atrium receives freshly oxygenated blood returning from the lungs through the four pulmonary veins, before passing it to the left ventricle.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The circle of Willis, an anastomotic ring of arteries, is located at the base of which organ?
questions.explanation: The circle of Willis is an arterial anastomosis at the base of the brain, formed by the internal carotid and vertebrobasilar systems, providing collateral circulation to the brain.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which cranial nerve is responsible for the sense of smell?
questions.explanation: The olfactory nerve (Cranial Nerve I) carries sensory information for the sense of smell from the nasal mucosa to the olfactory bulb.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The hepatorenal recess (Morison's pouch), a common site for fluid collection in a supine patient, lies between which two organs?
questions.explanation: Morison's pouch is the potential space between the posterior surface of the liver and the anterior surface of the right kidney, and is a dependent recess where free fluid commonly collects in supine patients.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which regions of the vertebral column normally show a lordotic (forward convex) curvature?
questions.explanation: The cervical and lumbar regions of the spine show normal secondary curvatures that are lordotic (concave posteriorly/convex anteriorly), while the thoracic and sacral curvatures are kyphotic.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The sternal (jugular) notch, used as a landmark for chest and neck positioning, corresponds to approximately which vertebral level?
questions.explanation: The suprasternal (jugular) notch, at the superior border of the manubrium, corresponds to approximately the T2–T3 vertebral level.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which structure separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity?
questions.explanation: The diaphragm is the dome-shaped musculotendinous structure that separates the thoracic cavity above from the abdominal cavity below.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The acetabulum, which articulates with the head of the femur to form the hip joint, is formed by the fusion of which three bones?
questions.explanation: The acetabulum is a cup-shaped socket on the lateral pelvis formed by the fusion of the three pelvic bones — the ilium, ischium and pubis.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Cardiac output is calculated as the product of heart rate and which other variable?
questions.explanation: Cardiac output (volume of blood pumped per minute) = Heart rate × Stroke volume (the volume ejected per beat).

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which lobe of the liver is the largest?
questions.explanation: The right lobe is the largest lobe of the liver, considerably bigger than the left, caudate and quadrate lobes.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The greater trochanter, an important bony landmark for hip and femoral neck positioning, is located on which bone?
questions.explanation: The greater trochanter is a large bony prominence on the proximal lateral surface of the femur, palpable and used as a landmark for hip positioning.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The shoulder (glenohumeral) joint, which allows the widest range of motion of any joint in the body, is classified as which type of joint?
questions.explanation: The glenohumeral (shoulder) joint is a ball-and-socket synovial joint, formed by the head of the humerus articulating with the glenoid cavity of the scapula, permitting motion in multiple planes.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The spinal cord typically terminates (as the conus medullaris) at approximately which vertebral level in an adult?
questions.explanation: In an adult, the spinal cord tapers into the conus medullaris and typically terminates at approximately the L1–L2 vertebral level, below which lies the cauda equina.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which blood vessels return deoxygenated blood from the body into the right atrium?
questions.explanation: The superior vena cava (from the upper body) and the inferior vena cava (from the lower body) are the two great veins that empty deoxygenated blood into the right atrium.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The costophrenic angle, routinely assessed for blunting on a chest radiograph, is formed at the junction of the diaphragm and which structure?
questions.explanation: The costophrenic angle is the sharp angle formed where the diaphragm meets the lateral rib cage/chest wall; blunting of this angle on a chest X-ray suggests pleural effusion.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: Which type of necrosis is characteristically seen in tuberculosis, appearing as a cheese-like, friable material?
questions.explanation: Caseous necrosis, typically caused by mycobacterial infection (TB), produces a soft, cheese-like, friable material composed of dead tissue and is a combination of coagulative and liquefactive necrosis.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: The suffix '-oma' in medical terminology generally denotes:
questions.explanation: The suffix '-oma' generally means a tumour or swelling, as in 'adenoma', 'lipoma' or 'carcinoma'.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: Which of the following is a cardinal sign of acute inflammation?
questions.explanation: The classical cardinal signs of acute inflammation are rubor (redness), calor (heat), tumor (swelling), dolor (pain) and functio laesa (loss of function).

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: A benign tumour arising from glandular epithelial tissue is termed:
questions.explanation: A benign tumour of glandular epithelial origin is called an 'adenoma'; its malignant counterpart is called an 'adenocarcinoma'.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: As per Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, which colour-coded bag is used for the disposal of human anatomical waste such as body parts and tissues?
questions.explanation: Under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, yellow bags/containers are designated for human anatomical waste, soiled waste, and expired or discarded medicines, meant for incineration or deep burial.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: Coagulative necrosis, in which the basic tissue architecture is preserved for several days, is most typically seen following:
questions.explanation: Coagulative necrosis is the characteristic pattern of necrosis in solid organs following ischemia, classically seen in myocardial infarction, where the tissue outline is preserved for some days before it is cleared.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: The voluntary, written permission obtained from a patient before an invasive procedure such as an IVU is called:
questions.explanation: Informed consent is the process of obtaining a patient's voluntary agreement for a procedure after explaining its nature, risks, benefits and alternatives, typically documented in writing before invasive investigations.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: A malignant tumour arising from connective tissue such as bone, muscle or fat is termed:
questions.explanation: Malignant tumours of mesenchymal (connective tissue) origin — including bone, cartilage, muscle and fat — are termed 'sarcomas', in contrast to 'carcinomas' which arise from epithelial tissue.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: A patient develops sudden breathlessness, hypotension and urticaria immediately after IV contrast injection. What is the immediate first step?
options: Ask the patient to walk around
Stop the contrast injection immediately and call for emergency assistance
questions.explanation: On recognising signs of a severe/anaphylactoid contrast reaction, the immediate first step is to stop the contrast administration at once, call for emergency help, and initiate resuscitation as per the department's emergency protocol.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: Necrotic tissue that is enzymatically digested to become soft and liquefied, commonly seen in the brain after infarction, is termed:
questions.explanation: Liquefactive necrosis occurs when dead tissue is digested by enzymes and transformed into a liquid, viscous mass; it is the typical pattern seen in cerebral infarcts and pyogenic bacterial infections.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: Treating all blood and body fluids as potentially infectious, regardless of a patient's known status, is the core principle of:
questions.explanation: Standard (universal) precautions require healthcare workers to treat all patients' blood and body fluids as potentially infectious, using appropriate barrier protection at all times.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: As per Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, which colour-coded bag is used for general, non-hazardous solid waste in a healthcare facility?
questions.explanation: Black bags/containers are used for general, non-hazardous solid waste (such as domestic-type refuse) that does not require special treatment prior to disposal.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: A patient's right to be informed about the risks, benefits and alternatives of a procedure before agreeing to it is known as:
options: The right to a second opinion
questions.explanation: The right to informed consent obligates healthcare providers to disclose relevant information about a procedure so the patient can make a voluntary, informed decision before agreeing to it.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: Metastasis refers to:
options: The complete cure of a tumour after treatment
The formation of a benign cyst
The abnormal enlargement of an organ
The spread of malignant cells from the primary site to distant parts of the body
questions.explanation: Metastasis is the process by which malignant (cancerous) cells spread from their primary site of origin to distant tissues or organs via blood, lymphatics or direct seeding.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: Which sterilization method, using high-pressure saturated steam, is most commonly used for surgical and radiological instruments?
questions.explanation: Autoclaving uses high-pressure saturated steam (typically 121–134°C) to achieve reliable sterilization of reusable surgical and diagnostic instruments.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: Gangrene that develops with a superimposed bacterial infection, producing foul smell, swelling and systemic toxicity, is termed:
questions.explanation: Wet gangrene occurs when ischemic/necrotic tissue is invaded by putrefying bacteria, producing swelling, a foul odour and rapid spread, as opposed to dry gangrene which is a slower, mummifying process.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: Which of the following is considered the single most effective measure to prevent healthcare-associated infections?
options: Wearing a mask at all times
questions.explanation: Proper hand hygiene — using alcohol-based hand rub or soap and water — is widely recognised as the single most effective and cost-efficient measure to prevent the spread of healthcare-associated infections.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: The legal and ethical duty to keep a patient's medical and imaging records private is known as:
questions.explanation: Confidentiality refers to the healthcare provider's ethical and legal obligation not to disclose a patient's medical information without proper authorisation.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: Dysplasia refers to:
options: Abnormal changes in cell size, shape and organisation, often considered a pre-cancerous change
The complete absence of an organ at birth
questions.explanation: Dysplasia describes disordered growth marked by variation in cell size, shape and arrangement; it is often reversible but can be a precursor to malignant change if the underlying stimulus persists.

questions.subject: Pathology & Patient Care
questions.question: As per Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, sharps such as needles and blades should be disposed of in which type of container?
questions.explanation: Sharps, including needles, syringes with fixed needles and other metallic sharps, are disposed of in white translucent, puncture-proof containers as per the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: On a T1-weighted MR image, fat appears:
questions.explanation: Fat has a short T1 relaxation time, causing it to recover its longitudinal magnetization quickly and appear bright (hyperintense) on T1-weighted images.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: On a T2-weighted MR image, water and CSF appear:
questions.explanation: Water and CSF have long T2 relaxation times, retaining transverse magnetization longer, which makes them appear bright (hyperintense) on T2-weighted images.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: Gadolinium-based contrast agents used in MRI primarily shorten which relaxation time, increasing signal on T1-weighted images?
questions.explanation: Gadolinium is paramagnetic and predominantly shortens the T1 relaxation time of nearby water protons, producing increased (bright) signal on T1-weighted post-contrast images.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: In MRI safety zoning, Zone IV refers to:
options: The MRI scanner (magnet) room itself, where the field is always on
questions.explanation: Zone IV is the MRI scanner room, where the static magnetic field is always present and access is restricted to specifically screened personnel and patients.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: The repetition time (TR) in an MRI pulse sequence primarily controls the amount of:
questions.explanation: TR (repetition time), the interval between successive excitation pulses, primarily governs the degree of T1 relaxation/weighting that is allowed to occur before the next pulse.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: The echo time (TE) in an MRI pulse sequence primarily controls the amount of:
questions.explanation: TE (echo time), the time between excitation and signal readout, primarily determines the degree of T2 relaxation/weighting reflected in the resulting image.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: What Hounsfield Unit (HU) value is assigned to water on a CT scan?
questions.explanation: The Hounsfield scale is calibrated such that distilled water is defined as 0 HU, serving as the reference point of the scale.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: What is the approximate Hounsfield Unit (HU) value of air on a CT scan?
questions.explanation: Air, being far less attenuating than water, is assigned an HU value of approximately -1000 on the Hounsfield scale.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: In CT scanning, 'pitch' is defined as:
options: The angle of the gantry tilt
Table travel per gantry rotation divided by the total collimated beam width
questions.explanation: Pitch in helical/spiral CT is defined as the table movement per 360° gantry rotation divided by the total collimated (beam) width, describing how tightly or loosely the helix is wound.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: Which generation of CT scanners uses a rotating X-ray tube combined with a stationary 360° ring of detectors?
questions.explanation: Fourth-generation CT scanners use a 'rotate-stationary' geometry, where the X-ray tube rotates around the patient while the detectors form a fixed, stationary 360° ring.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: CTDIvol (CT Dose Index volume), a standard CT dose descriptor, is expressed in which unit?
questions.explanation: CTDIvol is a standardised measure of the average radiation dose within a scanned volume and is expressed in milligray (mGy).

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: Dose Length Product (DLP) is calculated by multiplying CTDIvol by:
questions.explanation: DLP = CTDIvol × scan length, providing an estimate of the total radiation energy delivered over the entire scanned length, expressed in mGy·cm.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: Which MRI artifact appears as a localised signal void with geometric distortion caused by metallic implants?
questions.explanation: Susceptibility artifacts arise from local magnetic field inhomogeneities caused by metallic objects, producing signal void and geometric distortion around the implant.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: The 'magic angle' artifact in MRI is most commonly encountered when imaging which type of structure?
questions.explanation: The magic angle effect causes an artefactual increase in signal in tightly bound collagenous tissues such as tendons when they are oriented at approximately 55° to the main magnetic field, and is a common pitfall in rotator cuff imaging.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: In CT imaging, the process of adjusting the displayed grey-scale range to optimally visualise a specific tissue (e.g., lung, bone or soft tissue) is called:
questions.explanation: Windowing refers to adjusting the window width and window level to select the grey-scale range of Hounsfield Units best suited to display a particular tissue type.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: Which MRI pulse sequence suppresses the signal from fat and is useful for detecting bone marrow oedema?
questions.explanation: STIR sequences use an inversion time tuned to null the signal from fat, making them highly sensitive for detecting bone marrow oedema and other fluid-related pathology.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: Which MRI pulse sequence suppresses the signal from fluid/CSF and is useful for detecting periventricular white matter lesions in multiple sclerosis?
questions.explanation: FLAIR nulls the signal from CSF using a long inversion time, making periventricular and juxtacortical white matter lesions, such as those in multiple sclerosis, much more conspicuous.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: In helical/multi-slice CT, increasing the pitch beyond 1 generally results in:
options: Faster scanning with reduced dose but slightly reduced z-axis resolution
No effect on scan time or dose
Improved spatial resolution with higher dose
questions.explanation: A pitch greater than 1 means the table moves faster relative to the beam width per rotation, covering more anatomy per unit time and reducing dose, at some cost to z-axis (longitudinal) resolution.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: A ferromagnetic object being pulled uncontrollably towards the MRI magnet bore is known as the:
questions.explanation: The projectile (missile) effect describes the powerful, uncontrolled attraction of ferromagnetic objects towards the MRI magnet, a major safety hazard in and around the scanner room.

questions.subject: MRI & CT Imaging
questions.question: Which relaxation process in MRI refers to the recovery of longitudinal magnetization?
questions.explanation: T1 relaxation, also called spin-lattice relaxation, describes the recovery of longitudinal magnetization as excited protons transfer energy to the surrounding lattice.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: What is the SI unit of absorbed radiation dose?
questions.explanation: The Gray (Gy) is the SI unit of absorbed dose, defined as one joule of radiation energy absorbed per kilogram of tissue.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: What is the SI unit of equivalent (effective) radiation dose?
questions.explanation: The Sievert (Sv) is the SI unit of equivalent/effective dose, which accounts for the biological effectiveness of different types of radiation.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: What is the SI unit of radioactivity?
questions.explanation: The Becquerel (Bq) is the SI unit of radioactivity, defined as one nuclear disintegration per second.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: As per AERB norms, what is the annual occupational dose limit for a radiation worker (averaged over 5 consecutive years)?
questions.explanation: As per AERB regulations, occupational radiation workers are limited to an average effective dose of 20 mSv per year over any defined 5 consecutive years, with a maximum of 30 mSv in any single year.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: Half Value Layer (HVL) is defined as the thickness of a material required to reduce the intensity of an X-ray beam to:
options: A quarter of its original value
questions.explanation: HVL is defined as the thickness of a specified absorbing material needed to reduce the intensity of an X-ray beam to exactly half (50%) of its original (unattenuated) value.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: TLD (Thermoluminescent Dosimeter) personnel monitoring badges are most commonly made using which crystal material?
questions.explanation: Lithium fluoride (LiF) is the crystal material most commonly used in TLD badges, releasing light proportional to the absorbed radiation dose when heated.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: The principle of ALARA in radiation protection stands for:
questions.explanation: ALARA is a foundational radiation safety principle stating that radiation exposure should be kept 'As Low As Reasonably Achievable', considering economic and social factors.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: Increasing the kVp in an X-ray exposure primarily affects:
options: The penetrating power (quality) and energy of the X-ray beam
Only the quantity of X-rays, not their energy
questions.explanation: kVp controls the peak energy of the X-ray photons produced, thereby determining the beam's penetrating power (quality) and influencing image contrast.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: Increasing the mAs in an X-ray exposure primarily affects:
options: The quantity (number) of X-ray photons produced
The energy of individual X-ray photons
questions.explanation: mAs (milliampere-seconds) controls the total number of electrons flowing through the tube and hence the quantity of X-ray photons produced, directly affecting image density/radiographic exposure, without changing photon energy.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: The main function of an anti-scatter grid in radiography is to:
options: Absorb scattered radiation and improve image contrast
questions.explanation: An anti-scatter grid is placed between the patient and the image receptor to absorb obliquely travelling scattered radiation before it reaches the detector, thereby improving image contrast.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: The anode heel effect in X-ray tube design results in:
options: Higher intensity only at the centre of the field
Uniform intensity across the entire field
Variation in beam intensity across the field, with higher intensity on the cathode side
questions.explanation: The anode heel effect causes greater attenuation of X-rays exiting toward the anode side due to the angled target, resulting in higher beam intensity on the cathode side of the field and lower intensity on the anode side.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: Which crystal material is most commonly used as the detector element in OSL (Optically Stimulated Luminescence) dosimetry badges?
questions.explanation: OSL badges (such as Luxel dosimeters) commonly use carbon-doped aluminium oxide (Al2O3:C) crystals, which release light proportional to absorbed dose when stimulated by laser light.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: The deterministic effect of radiation exposure, which has a threshold dose and increases in severity with increasing dose, is exemplified by:
questions.explanation: Deterministic effects, such as skin erythema and cataract formation, occur only above a threshold dose, and their severity increases as the dose increases further; cancer and genetic effects are stochastic, not deterministic.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: Stochastic effects of radiation, such as cancer induction, are characterised by:
options: A definite threshold dose below which they never occur
Probability of occurrence increases with dose, but severity is independent of dose (no threshold)
Immediate onset within hours of exposure
questions.explanation: Stochastic effects have no dose threshold; the probability of the effect occurring increases with dose, but the severity of the effect (once it occurs) does not depend on the dose received.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: The three cardinal principles of radiation protection are time, distance and:
questions.explanation: The three fundamental principles for minimising radiation exposure are minimising time of exposure, maximising distance from the source, and using appropriate shielding.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: In Computed Radiography (CR), the X-ray image is initially captured on a:
questions.explanation: In CR systems, the latent image is stored on a photostimulable phosphor (PSP) plate, which is later scanned by a laser reader to release the stored energy as light and generate the digital image.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: In Direct Digital Radiography (DR), X-rays are converted into an electronic image using:
options: A photostimulable phosphor plate that requires separate scanning
questions.explanation: DR systems use a flat-panel detector (direct or indirect conversion type) that converts X-ray energy into an electronic signal instantly, without the need for a separate cassette-scanning step as in CR.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: What is the commonly recommended lead-equivalent thickness for a standard protective apron used in diagnostic radiography?
questions.explanation: Standard protective aprons used in diagnostic radiography typically provide a lead-equivalent protection of 0.25 mm to 0.5 mm, sufficient to substantially attenuate scattered radiation at diagnostic energies.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: Filtration of the X-ray beam (using added aluminium filters) primarily serves to:
options: Remove low-energy (soft) X-rays that would otherwise be absorbed by the patient without contributing to the image
Increase the total number of X-ray photons produced
Focus the beam to a smaller area
questions.explanation: Added filtration (commonly aluminium) preferentially absorbs low-energy, non-penetrating photons that would otherwise contribute only to patient skin dose without reaching the image receptor, thereby reducing patient dose while hardening the beam.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & Safety
questions.question: As per AERB regulations, what is the annual effective dose limit for members of the general public?
questions.explanation: AERB regulations limit the annual effective dose to members of the general public (non-occupationally exposed persons) to 1 mSv per year.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: What is the typical frequency range of transducers used in diagnostic medical ultrasound?
questions.explanation: Diagnostic ultrasound transducers typically operate in the range of about 2 to 15 MHz (occasionally up to ~18-20 MHz for superficial structures), well above the range of audible sound.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: In ultrasound imaging, higher-frequency transducers provide:
options: No change in resolution or penetration
Better resolution but lower penetration depth
Both better resolution and better penetration
questions.explanation: Higher-frequency ultrasound waves are attenuated more rapidly by tissue, limiting their penetration depth, but their shorter wavelength provides superior spatial resolution for superficial structures.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: The Doppler effect in ultrasound refers to:
options: The conversion of sound into electrical energy
The reflection of ultrasound at tissue interfaces
The absorption of ultrasound energy by bone
The change in frequency of reflected sound waves due to relative motion between the transducer and moving structures like blood
questions.explanation: The Doppler effect is the shift in frequency of ultrasound waves reflected from a moving target (such as flowing blood) relative to the transmitted frequency, and is the physical basis of Doppler ultrasound used to assess blood flow.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: In screening mammography, what are the two standard views obtained for each breast?
questions.explanation: Standard screening mammography includes the Craniocaudal (CC) view, taken from above, and the Mediolateral Oblique (MLO) view, which together image the greatest volume of breast tissue including the axillary tail.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: In the BI-RADS mammography reporting system, Category 5 indicates:
questions.explanation: BI-RADS Category 5 denotes findings that are highly suggestive of malignancy (≥95% likelihood of cancer), warranting appropriate biopsy/action.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: Which target–filter combination is most commonly used in conventional (screen-film/CR) mammography X-ray tubes?
questions.explanation: Conventional mammography X-ray tubes classically use a molybdenum target with a molybdenum filter (Mo/Mo), producing characteristic low-energy X-rays well suited to imaging soft breast tissue (rhodium is also used as an alternate target/filter for denser breasts).

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: An Intravenous Urogram (IVU) is primarily used to assess which organ system?
options: The urinary tract (kidneys, ureters and bladder)
questions.explanation: IVU (intravenous urography) uses an intravenously injected iodinated contrast agent excreted by the kidneys to outline and assess the anatomy and function of the kidneys, ureters and bladder.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: Barium sulfate, used as a contrast agent in GI studies, is contraindicated in cases of suspected:
questions.explanation: Barium sulfate is contraindicated when bowel perforation is suspected, as leakage of barium into the peritoneal cavity can cause severe peritonitis; a water-soluble iodinated contrast is used instead in such cases.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: A contrast reaction characterised by mild hives, itching and slight nausea, typically not requiring emergency intervention, is classified as:
questions.explanation: Mild contrast reactions (limited urticaria, itching, mild nausea) are usually self-limiting and require only observation and reassurance, unlike severe/anaphylactoid reactions which need immediate emergency management.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: The Seldinger technique is a standard method used for:
options: Positioning the patient for a barium enema
questions.explanation: The Seldinger technique is the standard percutaneous method for gaining vascular access using a needle, guidewire and catheter, forming the basis of most angiographic and interventional vascular procedures.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: A gamma camera used in nuclear medicine primarily detects radiation emitted from:
questions.explanation: A gamma camera detects gamma photons emitted from radioactive tracers (radiopharmaceuticals) that have been administered to and distributed within the patient, forming the basis of nuclear medicine imaging.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: Technetium-99m, the most commonly used radioisotope in nuclear medicine, has a physical half-life of approximately:
questions.explanation: Technetium-99m has a physical half-life of approximately 6 hours, short enough to minimise patient dose while long enough to allow imaging after tracer preparation and uptake.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: PET (Positron Emission Tomography) imaging commonly uses which radiopharmaceutical to assess tissue metabolic activity?
questions.explanation: F-18 labelled FDG (fluorodeoxyglucose), a glucose analogue, is the most widely used PET radiopharmaceutical, as its uptake reflects the metabolic (glycolytic) activity of tissues, particularly useful in oncology.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: The external beam radiotherapy technique that delivers radiation from multiple angles converging on the tumour while sparing surrounding tissue is broadly known as:
questions.explanation: Conformal (multi-field) external beam radiotherapy directs radiation beams from several different angles that converge on the tumour target, maximising the dose to the tumour while minimising exposure of surrounding normal tissue.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: The acoustic phenomenon in ultrasound where increased through-transmission of sound is seen distal to a fluid-filled structure (such as a simple cyst) is called:
questions.explanation: Because fluid attenuates ultrasound far less than surrounding solid tissue, the beam passing through a fluid-filled structure (like a cyst) loses less energy, resulting in a bright zone of increased through-transmission — posterior acoustic enhancement — deep to it.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: The dark shadow seen distal to a strongly attenuating or reflecting structure, such as a gallstone, on ultrasound is called:
questions.explanation: Highly attenuating or reflective structures such as gallstones or calcifications block most of the ultrasound beam from passing through, producing a dark shadow directly behind them, called acoustic (posterior) shadowing.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: The Mediolateral Oblique (MLO) view in mammography is typically angled at approximately:
questions.explanation: The MLO view is angled to follow the natural orientation of the pectoralis major muscle, typically around 30–60 degrees (commonly ~45 degrees), allowing the maximum volume of breast tissue, including the axillary tail, to be imaged.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: Which type of iodinated contrast media carries a lower risk of adverse reactions due to its lower osmolality compared to older ionic agents?
questions.explanation: Non-ionic, low-osmolar contrast media dissociate less in solution and have osmolality closer to blood plasma, resulting in a significantly lower incidence of adverse reactions compared to older high-osmolar ionic agents.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: In a standard femoral approach to angiography, the catheter is most commonly introduced via which artery?
questions.explanation: The common femoral artery is the most commonly used access site for angiographic and interventional procedures because of its relatively superficial location and large calibre, allowing easy compression for haemostasis afterward.

questions.subject: USG, Mammography & Special Procedures
questions.question: SPECT (Single Photon Emission Computed Tomography) differs from planar nuclear medicine imaging in that it provides:
options: A single flat 2D projection image only
Images without the need for a radiopharmaceutical
questions.explanation: Unlike planar imaging, which produces a single flat 2D projection, SPECT uses a rotating gamma camera to acquire multiple projections that are reconstructed into three-dimensional, cross-sectional tomographic images.
